evals.prompt: Quickly find what the default timeout behaviour of the Python requests library is.
evals.expected_output: A cheap lite search with highlights and no full text, answered from the excerpts with the source URL.
expectations: The answer cites at least one result URL
No exa_research_async.py, deep, or agent call is made for this lookup

evals.prompt: Using only exa.ai pages, what is Exa Lite and how much does it cost? Cite sources.
evals.expected_output: A cited answer whose every source is on exa.ai, produced via exa_research.py --domains exa.ai (routed to /search) or exa_search.py --domains exa.ai.
expectations: Every cited URL is on exa.ai
The answer states the $4 per 1,000 requests price

evals.prompt: Build me a list of 8 AI infrastructure startups that announced a Series A in 2026, with CEO and headquarters.
evals.expected_output: An exa_agent.py run with a bounded schema (preset or custom with maxItems 8), an explicit effort, and grounded results.
expectations: exa_agent.py run is used rather than many manual searches
The schema is bounded (--max-items 8 or maxItems in the schema)
If --effort is auto or ultra, --max-cost is also passed
The reply reports the run's cost or effort tier

evals.prompt: Pull the key points about pricing from https://exa.ai/pricing and https://exa.ai/docs/admin/pricing.
evals.expected_output: exa_contents.py on both URLs with query-focused highlights; no deprecated highlight fields are sent.
expectations: exa_contents.py is invoked with both URLs in one call
The summary lists per-endpoint prices drawn from the pages

evals.prompt: Cheaply get a one-sentence answer: who maintains the Python requests library today?
evals.expected_output: A synthesized one-line answer via exa_search.py --text-output on the default auto type (or exa_research.py), never --lite combined with a schema flag.
expectations: The answer is one sentence and cites a source URL
